text:
India Ministry of External Affairs advises citizens against Russian military enlistment
The Indian Ministry of External Affairs has issued a written statement advising citizens against seeking enlistment in the Russian military, following cases of nationals attempting to switch citizenship for financial gain before seeking release.
New Delhi Issues Strict Warning Against Russian Military Enlistment
The Ministry of External Affairs released a formal written statement addressing the number of Indian nationals attempting to join the Russian armed forces. According to the advisory, multiple individuals have approached Indian authorities with requests to voluntarily renounce their Indian citizenship, acquire Russian passports, and subsequently enter military service.
Many of these individuals are driven by expectations of significant financial compensation. However, a significant portion of these recruits later contact Indian diplomatic missions to request assistance in securing their release from combat units.
New Delhi characterized this path as highly hazardous and strongly discouraged. The government warned citizens to evaluate the gravity of such actions and recognize the lethal dangers to which they expose themselves.
Casualties and Repatriation Statistics Since 2022
Official figures released alongside the warning outline the scope of Indian participation in the Russian military since 2022. A total of 227 Indian nationals have entered the Russian military ranks.
Out of that total, 139 individuals have successfully secured their discharge and returned home. Meanwhile, 51 Indian citizens have lost their lives in active combat operations.
The Indian government maintains continuous contact with Russian authorities to ensure the safety, welfare, and early release of all remaining Indian nationals currently serving within the Russian armed forces.
